dataset.description: The AFLACHECK research initiative is designed to take a comprehensive, interdisciplinary approach to assess and address the risks of aflatoxin (AFs) contamination in the dairy supply chain, ensuring safe and healthy products from farm to table continuum. The project aims to develop a decision support software tool, supported by Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly through machine learning (ML), to analyze large datasets related to AFs contamination at various stages of the dairy supply chain. This tool will analyze data to identify specific trends and anomalies that signify the potential risk of AFs contamination. By doing so, it will enable dairy producers to predict contamination risks and make decisions before reaching determined threshold levels. The AFLACHECK methodologies move beyond reactive testing to a proactive, risk-based approach that utilizes monitoring, sampling, and real-time data, representing a significant advancement in Food Safety Management Systems (FSMS). This approach will also provide a scientific basis for regulatory decision-making and the development of food safety and public health management strategies, including risk ranking and prioritization. The use of AI in FSMS is crucial for optimizing resources and enhancing the quality and cost-effectiveness of monitoring. It improves the reliability of predicting food safety hazards, reinforces food safety measures, and boosts operational efficiency, all while ensuring compliance with food safety regulations. Engaging stakeholders in the dairy industry will be a fundamental pillar of the AFLACHECK project. Additionally, we will establish a comprehensive data management plan to promote open science practices, prioritizing transparency, accessibility, and ethical management of research outputs. AFLACHECK’s objectives are aligned with the needs of the dairy industry and public health sectors, making them highly pertinent and impactful. AFLACHECK also aims to establish a new standard in a proactive, cost-effective, scientifically grounded self-control system. The proposed research is ambitious, innovative, and highly relevant, as AFM1 poses a significant public health risk, especially in areas with frequent AFs contamination in dairy feeds. This interdisciplinary approach could transform dairy industry practices and enhance food safety in Serbia and beyond.

distribution.title: The AFLACHECK project will create the following types of data: 1.Analytical Data: Results of laboratory tests showing AFs contamination in feed ingredients, raw milk. 2. Modeling Data. 3. Animal welfare survey data including productivity. 4. Documentation and Software, reports related to data analysis, modeling, and decision support tools. The project will store data in open-access repositories, mainly Zenodo. All datasets will receive Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs) for persistent referencing. The project will make data available without restrictions to researchers, policymakers, and stakeholders through Zenodo and Cloud services (like OneDrive and Google Drive) for collaborative work. Access to sensitive datasets will be controlled with role-based permissions. The DMSP will be reviewed every six months to include new methods, tools, and regulations. The team will document changes and share them with all members to maintain compliance and consistency. The AFLACHECK project will also integrate the Serbian Open Science Platform 2.0 to enhance collaboration, resource sharing, and visibility of research outputs, further promoting transparency and open access in the management and sharing of data. By following this DMSP, the AFLACHECK project will effectively manage, ethically share, and preserve its data for the scientific community, stakeholders, and society.

dataset.title: AFLACHECK: Advanced artificial intelligence-driven tools for managing aflatoxins in the dairy supply chain

dmp.description: The AFLACHECK project aims to develop a simulation-based self-control and early warning system to prevent and manage aflatoxin M1 (AFM1) contamination in milk by integrating predictive modeling, risk-based monitoring, and real-time data analysis. It focuses on reducing human exposure, improving animal health and welfare, and supporting evidence-based food safety policies.
dmp.ethical_issues_description:
The research will be conducted in full compliance with relevant national and institutional guidelines for the care and use of animals. Ethical approval will be obtained from the appropriate Ethical Committee, ensuring that all procedures involving animals are ethically reviewed and authorized. We will provide the necessary documentation demonstrating that ethical and regulatory approval has been granted before the research begins. This includes adherence to animal welfare regulations and humane practices in all experimental procedures. The Ethical Committee's decision will serve as the formal authorization for the study to proceed.
We would also like to highlight that the project includes researchers from the Institute of Animal Husbandry in Zemun, who have received approval from their Ethics Committee (reference number 05-8084/13.12.2025). Additionally, the Ethics Committee of the Faculty of Agriculture at the University of Belgrade has provided their opinion, documented under No. 90/6-1/26.12.2024. We believe that this information, along with the provided clarification, is adequate for submitting the project proposal at this stage.All necessary documents are included and attached to the proposal.
